claims.text: The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy is a single-phase bulk high-entropy alloy with a homogeneous microstructure.
Under high-strain-rate monotonic tensile loading at room temperature, the dislocation generation rate exceeds dislocation mobility.
An imbalance between dislocation generation and mobility causes localized dislocation pile-ups.
High strain rates provide insufficient time for dislocations to redistribute.
Dislocation accumulation produces pronounced localized slip bands.
Dislocation pile-ups create local stress concentrations around slip bands.
Stress concentrations associated with pile-ups trigger microcrack initiation along slip bands.
Pile-up-associated microcrack initiation promotes brittle-like crack propagation and fracture.
The proposed high-strain-rate failure process reduces the alloy's toughness.
Under low-strain-rate loading, the alloy has a homogeneous dislocation distribution and ductile fracture behavior.
Relative to low-rate loading, high-rate loading will produce more localized slip bands and dislocation pile-ups.
Dislocation pile-up is expected to dominate failure at high strain rates over twinning or localized amorphous-band formation.
High-resolution TEM can distinguish pile-up-dominated failure from failure dominated by twinning or localized amorphous bands.
The proposed behavior is applicable primarily to room-temperature service involving rapid loading or impact.
